A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the creep strain path in the solder joints is more complex than the strain path in the thermomechanical cycled specimens, and the anisotropies of Sn are important in the creep process but not as significant in the thermomechancial cycled specimens.

the anisotropic nature of the solder and the slip systems that are active in the creep and thermomechanical fatigue processes lead to the development of a complex microstructure and crystal orientation distribution that ultimately leads to failure.
the anisotropic behavior of the solder is the primary reason for the different failure mechanisms and the different failure times.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anisotropies of Sn and the slip systems in the solder are important to the evolution of crystallographic texture and microstructure and to the ultimate failure of surface-mount solder joints.
a combination of the anisotropic properties of tin and the crystallography of the microstructure of eutectic solder joints can account for the observed crystal rotations and failure of these joints.
